Closes #2332.

## What's changing, and why

Three rough edges advisors hit the day 0.47.0 shipped are smoothed out.

- **A cloud check's result is always readable.** Neither host can read a cloud check session's own log, so starting a check now requires an issue for the session to post its one result line on. A check with no issue, or one whose issue cannot be read, is refused before anything starts. Advisors no longer start a check, find nothing to read, and re-run it with `--issue`. The set-up page and both host tool maps say the same.
- **A leftover finding is recognised under one normalisation.** The rule that every finding left for the owner is named under `## What we're accepting` used to match the record id and title byte for byte, so a title quoted with different punctuation or quotes was refused. Ids now match case-insensitively as a whole word (dashes unified, surrounding punctuation ignored), and titles ignore case, quotes, punctuation and underscore emphasis. Two different leftovers are never satisfied by one line: when two ids of one review would read the same under that rule (`f-1` and `f-1_`, `f-1.`, `(f-1)`, or a double space), each is matched on its exact bytes, and an id that sits inside a longer such id does not count.
- **A finding fixed by a higher layer of the same stack has its own disposition.** Instead of an "accepting" line that reads as if the owner accepts a defect, the line can say `fixed-above #<layer PR> <commit>`. Both the builder's ready check and the advisor's READY write accept it only when the named PR is a higher member of the same stack, and refuse it when the stack cannot be read. On a stack sheet the finding shows under what the review caught, as fixed above, not as accepted.

## What we're accepting

- plugins/superheroes/lib/leftover_accepting.py::exercise nfkc normalization together with punctuation stripping@L134 Exercise NFKC normalization together with punctuation stripping — merging accepts that an acceptance line wrapping an id in full-width punctuation (for example `（Ｆ－１）` or a full-width colon) is refused until it is rewritten in ordinary punctuation; the refusal names the finding. The test role's test for this (`test_leftover_nfkc_wrappers_2332.py`) reproduces it and is not in the PR.
- plugins/superheroes/lib/tests/test_pr_sheet_fixed_above_2332.py::claimtest mismatch unmatched disposition is not proved harmless@L166 claim/test mismatch: unmatched disposition is not proved harmless — merging accepts one sheet test that checks only one of the problems its fixture raises, so a later change that also refused an unmatched fixed-above line could pass it.
- The second review session ended `cannot-certify`: the test role's break-it test for the full-width finding above reproduces the bug and was not kept, because that finding is left for the owner rather than fixed. Every planned seat ran in that session, and its review record reads `awaits-owner` (its only open lines are the two findings above).
- Partial sweep coverage: the four searchers of sweep S-1 used targeted search over about 620 files each instead of reading every file, so the sweep for the pattern "untested refusal boundary" is not a full-coverage clearance.
- Order C's final text was not re-run through the semantic order lint after its Minor finding was folded in (the deterministic lint did re-run), so the last edit to that order was not checked by the semantic seat.

N/A — say it: no screen changes. The changes show up as wording: a new refusal when a cloud check starts without an issue, a looser leftover match, and a new `fixed-above` disposition word.

**Why it goes back.**
- **Leftovers can still be miscounted, by a different route.** You asked that one line under "What we're accepting" never count for two different findings. It still can, when one finding's id shows up inside the other finding's line once capitals or punctuation are ignored. For example, a line about `f-1 b` also counts for a separate finding `F-1`. The second finding is then never put to you on its own line. The old rule refused these cases, so this PR would make the check looser where you asked it not to be.
- **The page says otherwise.** This PR's description says that can never happen.
- **The fix closes it for good.** Each line counts for one finding at most. A line that names two findings counts for one, and the check asks for a line for the other. **What accepting it means.** Nothing yet: it is not up for merge. After the fix you will still carry two things:
- **The commit is not checked by any command.** The commit named in a `fixed-above` line is checked by the advisor at vet, not by the commands.
- **The result posts publicly.** A cloud check's result line is posted as a comment on the issue named, which is public on a public repository. It holds versions and a date, never the pass.

Two calls I made that you can take back:
- **Each line counts for one finding at most.** This is how to meet your rule. It is the third fix to the same matching code, so I set the shape rather than ordering another patch.
